title: EPFO CBT Meeting: Key Discussions on EPS & Retirement Withdrawals
description: The Employees' Provident Fund Organisation's Central Board of Trustees (CBT) is convening today, November 19, 2026, in New Delhi. A primary item on the agenda.

faq.a: The EPFO Central Board of Trustees (CBT) is the apex decision-making body of the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation. It comprises representatives from the government, employers, and employees, responsible for governing the schemes administered by EPFO.

EPS stands for Employees' Pension Scheme, 1995. It is a social security scheme administered by EPFO that provides a monthly pension to EPF subscribers upon retirement at age 58, or to their family in case of the subscriber's demise.

faq.q: What is the current minimum EPS pension?
faq.a: As of now, the minimum monthly pension under the Employees' Pension Scheme (EPS) is ₹1,000. This amount has been a subject of discussion for an upward revision due to rising living costs.

faq.q: Can I withdraw my EPF before retirement?
faq.a: Yes, partial withdrawals are allowed for specific purposes like house construction, education, marriage, or medical emergencies, under certain conditions and after a minimum service period. Full withdrawal is generally permitted only upon retirement (after 58 years) or prolonged unemployment.

faq.q: How do I check my EPF balance?
faq.a: You can check your EPF balance by logging into the EPFO member portal (https://epfindia.gov.in) using your Universal Account Number (UAN) and password, or through the UMANG app, or by sending an SMS to 7738299899.

faq.q: Will my employer contribution increase if EPS pension increases?
faq.a: An increase in the minimum EPS pension typically does not directly lead to an increase in the employer's contribution rate to EPF. The employer's contribution to EPS is a fixed percentage (8.33%) of the basic wage, capped at ₹15,000.

No, the discussions at the CBT meeting are proposals. Any changes to the minimum EPS pension or withdrawal rules would need to be approved by the CBT and subsequently notified by the Ministry of Labour and Employment or the Ministry of Finance to come into effect.
